expectations.text: Produces at least one markdown specification file in the assigned output directory.
Includes a clarification section with questions, assumptions, or confirmed understanding before finalizing the spec.
expectations.evidence: Includes open questions and assumptions with confidence/invalidation detail.

expectations.text: Includes stable agent-readable sections for summary/problem, scope or non-goals, requirements, acceptance criteria, verification, and open questions.
expectations.evidence: Includes summary, problem statement, goals, non-goals, requirements, testing and verification, open questions, assumptions, and acceptance criteria.

expectations.text: Uses requirement identifiers or another stable numbering convention that downstream agents can reference.
Acceptance criteria are concrete enough to verify through file inspection, tests, commands, or scripted checks.
expectations.evidence: Acceptance criteria mention implementing `.context/agent-memory.md`, required sections, promotion/exclusion rules, source pointers, line-count checks, and no prohibited files.

expectations.text: Mentions relevant existing workspace context such as current skills, docs, or instruction files based on read-only inspection.
expectations.evidence: Source context cites defining-specifications, engineering-context, session-retrospective, ticket-workflow, and outcome schema files.

expectations.text: Converts a broad idea into one focused spec rather than producing a broad documentation rewrite or downstream ticket set.
expectations.evidence: The spec focuses on `.context/agent-memory.md` and explicitly excludes tickets, implementation code, hooks, embeddings, databases, and broad docs rewrites.

uncertainties: Timing/token metrics were unavailable from subagent notifications.
